thread:
maria: quick heads-up — I'm seeing the Go SDK sampleapp generator stream not respecting ctx cancel when an auth refresh happens mid-stream.

maria: Minimal repro below, trimmed: 
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
stream, err := client.Generators.Generate(ctx, req)
// background token refresher may rotate token
// caller does cancel()
cancel()
for chunk := range stream.Chunks() {
  fmt.Println(chunk) // still prints for several seconds after cancel
}
```

maria: Logs show 401 -> refresh -> retry and the retry path seems to continue delivering chunks even after ctx.Err() != nil.

sam: is the refresher swapping headers on the transport (RoundTripper) or doing a synchronous refresh inside the request goroutine?

maria: sampleapp uses a transport wrapper that swaps the Authorization header when the token changes. The auth path triggers a retry flow that creates a new http.Request. I think the new request doesn't carry the original ctx.

john: that matches past issues — if retry creates a fresh request with background context it won't be cancellable by the original ctx.

elaine: check runtime/http_client.go (or runtime.go) — are we using http.NewRequest without req.WithContext(origCtx) when rebuilding the request for retry?

maria: confirmed: retryAuth() in runtime.go constructs a new req and just sets headers; no WithContext. That would explain why cancel() doesn't stop the remote retry.

sam: Proposed quick fixes: 1) ensure any retried request uses origReq.Context() via req = req.WithContext(origCtx); 2) avoid performing blocking token refresh on the per-request goroutine — return a retriable error and let the higher-level retry orchestrator handle refresh.

john: long-term, we should centralize token refresh so it doesn't block request goroutines. Short-term patch can copy the ctx to the new request and add a unit test for cancel semantics.

elaine: I'll add a test in gen_integration_test that creates a fake auth server which delays a refresh and then assert that cancel() causes stream iteration to stop immediately. Covers the leak/regression.

maria: I'll open the PR with the minimal fix + test + a short doc note in the generator README about "do not do blocking refresh in per-request goroutines; either fail fast or refresh with separate ctx and reattach to original request ctx for retry."

ci-bot: buildkite: started pipeline #8912 for branch fix/ctx-cancel-auth-retry

maria: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/342 — includes: patch to copy ctx onto retry requests, unit test for streaming cancel during auth retry, README blurb, and a tiny sampleapp update showing timeout/cancel best practices.

sam: nit: add example showing context.WithTimeout tied to a user action, e.g. 2s deadline for interactive flows. Many users forget to attach deadlines.

john: also add a note in the devex onboarding guide: "Avoid inline blocking token refresh in request handlers; use a dedicated refresh mechanism so cancellations propagate."

elaine: code lgtm, left two small style nits. Tests prove the cancellation behavior is fixed.

maria: thanks — merging once CI green. Will follow up if dedicated test matrix finds related timing flakiness.

sam: thanks for catching this early, Maria. :thumbsup:
